item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
This object will be turned to a different position

[Image: 3D object made of cubes]

Which of these could be the object after being turned?
item.figure_description:
An isometric drawing of a three-dimensional solid composed of 4 identical unit cubes:
- In the upper horizontal layer, 3 cubes form an L-shape consisting of a corner cube at the back, one cube extending forward and to the left, and one cube extending forward and to the right.
- In the lower layer, a fourth cube is situated directly underneath the forward-left cube, creating a vertical column of 2 cubes on the left side of the object. The spaces directly beneath the back corner cube and the forward-right cube are empty.

The response options show four similar objects made of 4 cubes, drawn in the same isometric perspective:
- Option A: Three cubes form an L-shape in an upper layer (a corner cube at the back, one cube extending forward-left, and one extending forward-right). A fourth cube is in a lower layer, positioned stepped down in front of the forward-left cube.
- Option B: A vertical column of 2 cubes is located on the right side (front-right). In the upper layer, extending back and to the left from the top cube of this column is a cube, and extending back and to the right from that cube is a third cube, forming an L-shape of 3 cubes in the upper layer with the 2-cube column at one end.
- Option C: Three cubes form a shape in an upper layer stepping up from a single cube in a lower layer at the front-left.
- Option D: A vertical column of 2 cubes is located on the right side (front-right). In the upper layer, two cubes extend to the left.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem shows a net of a cube consisting of six square faces arranged in a cross. A vertical column of four squares has, from top to bottom: a square containing a solid black circle, a square containing an unfilled circle, a square containing a solid black triangle pointing upward, and a blank square. Flanking the second square (with the unfilled circle) are two additional blank squares, one to the left and one to the right.

The options show perspective views of a cube displaying three faces (top, front-left, and front-right):
- A: Top face has a solid black circle, front-left face has an upward-pointing black triangle, and front-right face has an unfilled circle.
- B: Top face has an unfilled circle, front-left face has an upward-pointing black triangle, and front-right face has a solid black circle.
- C: Top face has an unfilled circle, front-left face has a solid black circle, and front-right face is blank.
- D: Top face has an unfilled circle, front-left face is blank, and front-right face is blank.

reference_items.figure_description:
At the top of the item, a person is standing to the left of a three-dimensional solid made of 5 small identical cubes. The person is shown in side profile facing right toward the solid, with a horizontal dotted line extending from the person's eyes to the top-left cube of the solid. The solid is drawn in isometric projection and consists of:
- A central vertical column of 3 cubes.
- One cube attached to the back-right of the top cube of the column, at the same height as the top cube.
- One cube attached to the front-right of the middle cube of the column, extending forward toward the viewer at the middle height level.

The response options each show a flat 2D shape composed of connected unit squares:
- Option A: 4 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the left of the middle square.
- Option B: 4 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the right of the middle square.
- Option C: 5 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the left of the middle square and 1 square attached to the right of the top square.
- Option D: 5 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the left of the top square and 1 square attached to the right of the middle square.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Rectangle PQRS can be rotated (turned) onto rectangle UVST.

[Image: Rectangles UVST and PQRS]

What point is the center of rotation?
reference_items.figure_description: Two adjacent congruent rectangles forming an L-like shape. Rectangle UVST is oriented vertically, with vertices U (bottom left), V (bottom right), S (top right), and T (top left). Rectangle PQRS is oriented horizontally, extending to the right from the upper portion of rectangle UVST: vertex S is at the top left (shared with UVST), R is at the top right, Q is at the bottom right, and P is at the bottom left, lying on the vertical line segment SV between S and V. Each vertex is marked with a black dot.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A rectangular prism, with a length of 5 blocks, width of 4 blocks, and height of 3 blocks. There is a hole shown on the top of the rectangular prism. The hole is 2 blocks by 3 blocks and goes all the way through the shape.]

The figure above shows a shape made up of cubes that are all the same size. There is a hole all the way through the shape. How many cubes would be needed to fill the hole?
reference_items.figure_description: An isometric drawing of a 3D block shape constructed from identical unit cubes. The overall block is 5 cubes wide along the front, 4 cubes deep along the right side, and 3 cubes tall. In the center of the top face, there is a rectangular rectangular hole measuring 3 cubes wide by 2 cubes deep, bordered by a rim that is 1 cube wide on all four sides. The hole extends vertically straight down through the entire height of 3 cubes.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A machine has 100 candies and dispenses a candy when a lever is turned. The machine has the same number of blue, pink, yellow, and green candies all mixed together. Megan turned the lever and obtained a pink candy. Peter turned the lever next.

How likely is it that Peter will get a pink candy?

options.label: A
options.text: It is certain that his candy will be pink.

options.label: B
options.text: It is more likely than it was for Megan.

options.label: C
options.text: It is exactly as likely as it was for Megan.

options.label: D
options.text: It is less likely than it was for Megan.

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem shows a 3-D triangular prism resting horizontally on one rectangular face, with dashed lines indicating the three hidden edges. The options show four candidate nets:
- Option A: A central horizontal rectangle with an isosceles triangle attached to each vertical side, and another rectangle attached to the outer edge of each triangle angled upward, forming an open V-shape.
- Option B: Three congruent rectangles stacked vertically in a column, with two identical triangles attached to the right edges of the top and middle rectangles, both pointing right.
- Option C: Two congruent rectangles stacked vertically, each having a triangle attached to its left edge pointing left; a third rectangle extends to the right from the top rectangle, ending with a triangle pointing right.
- Option D: Three congruent rectangles stacked vertically in a column, with one triangle attached to the right edge of the top rectangle pointing right, and another triangle attached to the left edge of the bottom rectangle pointing left.
